message.content: Although an Leshy, Pebble Spring became immediately fascinated by the mortal settlements when they set foot in a city. They loves the nicely paved ground, the intricate bridges, and the most of all, they loved houses. The nicely layed out stone walls forming shelters from the weathers yet connect the earth with the stories from every family. They decided to learn the craft of housebuilding with the help of a touch of arcane magic from their self-made staff. At first, Pebble Spring struggled to understand the basic principles of masonry and carpentry. The mortals built their homes with such precision that it seemed almost magical to their woodland eyes. Each beam had to be cut at the exact angle to support the weight above. Each stone had to be shaped perfectly to fit alongside its neighbors without any gaps. Pebble Spring spent months just observing, watching the builders at work from behind the trees. They would sneak closer at night when the campfires dimmed and the workers rested. The moonlight cast long shadows across the construction sites, and Pebble Spring studied the patterns. They learned that the foundation was the most critical part of any structure. Without a solid base, even the most beautiful house would eventually collapse. This lesson resonated deeply with Pebble Spring, who understood the importance of roots in nature. They began experimenting with small structures in the forest clearing near the city. At first, their attempts were crude and wobbly, barely standing in a strong wind. The other Leshy in the area watched with curiosity and mild amusement. Pebble Spring did not care about their opinions and continued working diligently. Over time, the small huts grew sturdier and more elegant in design. The arcane magic from the staff helped in ways that pure physical labor could not. Pebble Spring could sense the natural flow of energy through stone and wood. They channeled this energy to reinforce joints and seal cracks before they formed. The houses they built became known for their unique blend of organic and architectural beauty. The villagers who had initially dismissed Pebble Spring as a mere woodland creature soon found themselves drawn to the remarkable structures rising from the forest edge and they began whispering among themselves about the spotty patterns of moss and lichen that grew across every surface.
